title: Guard every path that writes content
statement: Run blocking content checks on every path that writes content, hand edits included, and roll back any write that fails them.
example: Before its direct-edit path was guarded, one course's rework reintroduced 5 misconception phrasings, caught only by a manual sweep.
detail: A Grade 3 reading course's science misconception gate, as its re-approval package's compliance log records, guarded regeneration: a regenerated lesson whose truth-asserting text still held a Tier-1 (absolute-prohibition) phrase failed and, if the phrase outlasted refinement, was discarded and rolled back. The direct-edit path was not guarded at first, so a rework of the teaching moves done by direct edit reintroduced 5 Tier-1 phrasings, which a manual sweep caught and fixed. An edit guard then snapshotted each file, applied the edit, re-swept it and rolled back to the snapshot if the edit introduced a Tier-1 phrase, so that the sweep blocked shipping on both write paths and a hand edit could no longer leave such a phrase on disk. The check sits on the write itself, rather than on a rerun after the fact.
against: One incident in one course; the log reports no later edit that the guard rolled back, so how often it fires is unmeasured.

evidence.quote: Earlier in this effort the direct-edit path was NOT guarded, so the teaching-move rework transiently reintroduced 5 Tier-1 phrasings that were caught and fixed by a manual sweep
